evals.prompt: In this React component, fix the bug where changing the selected country does not clear the selected city. Keep the change small and follow nearby style.
evals.expected_output: Implements a narrow bug fix, prefers event-level or simple state flow over adding broad effects, and does not introduce generic form abstractions.

evals.prompt: Refactor src/features/users/UserForm.tsx to simplify the duplicated validation logic and run the relevant tests.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a concrete scoped refactor, edits directly after inspection, avoids a broad refactor plan gate, and keeps behavior unchanged.

evals.prompt: This dashboard frontend has become messy. Refactor the forms, tables, filters, and route structure so it is cleaner.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a broad refactor, inspects first, proposes a plan, states what will not be abstracted, and waits for confirmation before editing.

evals.prompt: Review this merge request that changes several React hooks and TypeScript form schemas. Focus on frontend code quality and regressions.
evals.expected_output: Responds in code-review mode with findings first, severity ordering, concrete file/line references where possible, risks, and testing gaps; avoids generic praise.

evals.prompt: Replace this hand-written grouping loop with the utility we already use in the app. The project has lodash-es imported elsewhere.
evals.expected_output: Reuses the existing utility dependency without adding a new dependency, checks local usage first, and only uses docs if API behavior is unclear or risky.

evals.prompt: Move this one-off JSX block into a shared configurable renderer because three fields look similar.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on premature abstraction, explains that direct JSX or small local structure is preferable unless the fields share behavior and real reuse.

evals.prompt: In this React Router app, refactor the route module for `/reports` so the loader/action data flow is easier to follow and the pending UI stays correct.
evals.expected_output: Applies frontend code-quality rules while recognizing that React Router-specific loader/action/navigation behavior should use the react-router skill when available. Keeps the refactor scoped and does not apply Next.js-specific patterns.

evals.prompt: Pouzi frontend-code-quality, ale v IQF projekte uprav FE Zod schemas pre monitoring modul podla aktualnych backend @View interfaces a DTO tried.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as IQF backend-to-frontend Zod schema mapping even though the user mentioned frontend-code-quality, and switches to iqf-fe-schema-generator when available instead of handling it as generic frontend code-quality work.
assertions: Does not proceed with IQF schema generation using only generic frontend-code-quality guidance.
Explicitly identifies the task as IQF backend-to-frontend Zod schema mapping.
Uses or defers to `iqf-fe-schema-generator` when that skill is available.
